content: Wealth acquired through deceit and unrighteousness burns like a fiery brand in the house of the thief.
author: Sanskrit Subhashitas
sourceWork: Adharmena edhate tavan (अधर्मेणैधते तावत्) — Classical Niti Maxim
explanation: Ill-gotten gains may provide temporary luxury, but they arrive accompanied by the invisible furies of paranoia, guilt, family discord, and moral ruin. What was stolen or swindled becomes the fire that consumes the roof. Clean bread in poverty is sweeter than honey stolen in shame.
practicalInsight: Never take an ethical shortcut for financial profit. Protect your clean conscience as your primary treasure.
reflectionPrompt: Where in your past did an ethical compromise bring a temporary advantage that ultimately burned your peace?
